Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning - appreciate you walking through Acme's expected traffic patterns. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key integration and dedicated-capacity sizing items and the next steps so we can align the Dedicated PO and internal infra folks.

Recap (integration & architecture topics we covered)
- SDK & auth: you’ll integrate via our python/java SDK; auth is token-based with optional mTLS for Private deployments. We flagged a short task to get your SREs a test token and the private CA info.
- Routing & routing policies: requests can be routed by region/latency/cost. For now we recommended pinning Acme to a dedicated pool in us-west.
- Structured output & tool-calling: we discussed using Redwood's structured output mode for your tool-calling pipeline (JSON schema enforcement + function calling). We’ll share the example schema.
- Embeddings & rerankers: we suggested local embeddings store + periodic re-rank job. We’ll share recommended vector dimensionality and suggested L2 vs cosine settings.

Dedicated capacity sizing notes (from the call)
- Typical request mix: 60% chat/generation (avg 220 tokens), 35% embeddings (batch size ~50), 5% rerank/query-time scoring.
- Peak qps: ~120 qps across endpoints, bursting to ~200 qps for short windows (~10-15 min).
- Concurrency: average concurrent generation calls ~350; peak concurrency observed by you historically ~620.
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 250ms for short prompts; up to 1s for longer context windows.
- Queueing: we recommended a front-door queue with target depth 1.5x peak concurrency and a backpressure policy for bursts.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Aditya (solutions engineer) - he’ll recommend autoscaling policies and exact GPU pod counts.
2) Share the sizing workbook (attached) + your historical traces (if you can).
3) Set up a short SRE auth/test token handoff so you can hit a staging pool.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (workbook with scenarios), acme-network-diagram.pdf (from Tom)

Can we target Wed 10/21 10:00am PT for the deep-dive? If that works, I’ll loop in Aditya and Dev to cover autoscaling and queueing strategy.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sarah / team - thanks for the details, and thanks Marissa for the agenda. A few technical notes I’ll bring to the deep-dive and preliminary recommendations based on the numbers you shared: 

1) Baseline pod count (GPU pods)
- For generation workload (60% of requests, avg 220 tokens): assuming A100-class pods with our optimized runtime, one pod can sustain ~110 qps at p95 <= 250ms for short prompts with batching. To hit 120 qps sustained we recommend 2 pods baseline to allow headroom for other workloads.
- Because you have bursts to 200 qps and high concurrency, add burst capacity via autoscaling to +3 pods (so up to 5 pods total) to cover burst windows.

2) Autoscaling policy
- Use target-based autoscaling on queue depth and p95 latency: scale up when queue depth > 0.7 * baseline_concurrency and p95 > 250ms for 2 consecutive minutes. Scale down after queue depth < 0.3 * baseline_concurrency for 5 minutes.
- Warm pool: keep 1 warm pod (cold start ~30s) for faster burst handling.

3) Queue sizing & routing
- Front-door queue depth target: 1.5x peak concurrency for your 620 peak => target queue depth ~930. But we prefer per-route configurable max_inflight with backpressure to avoid unbounded queues; set per-route inflight cap to 200 and use a small FIFO spillover queue with priority for low-latency endpoints.
- Suggest segregating endpoints: dedicated pool for generation, separate smaller pool for embeddings/rerankers (CPU/GPU mix) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

4) Batching & embeddings
- For embeddings batch size: 32 is fine; if you can increase to 64 that improves throughput but watch tail latency. We’ll run a quantization profile if you’re open to reduced-precision embeddings store to cut cost.

5) Auth & networking
- For Hosted Dedicated we’ll provide token + optional mTLS; for Private we’ll provide CA bundle and config. We’ll need your SREs to provision outbound IPs for allowlisting.

I’ll bring a worked example with pod counts and cost estimates to the call. Marissa - please share the sizing workbook and the traces.

Best,
